curated_comment: Kalanguya (ahin1234 = Ahin-Kayapa Kalanguya, ISO kak, Austronesian, Philippines) shows a Philippine-type voice/focus system with ergative alignment. GB409_1=1 (absolutive marker 'hi'/'i'), GB409_2-5=1 (all persons and full NPs have distinct absolutive/ergative forms). GB409_16=0 (topical A receives absolutive marking, the classic pivot construction), GB409_17=1 (non-topical A carries ergative marker 'ni'). GB409_6-13=1 (consistent across aspect/tense/mood). GB409_14=1 (agentive A takes ergative), GB409_18=1 (animate A ergative), GB409_21=1 (ergative in non-main clauses). GB409_22=1 (additional conditioning: recent perfective has special marking). GB409_23=1 (ergative marker 'ni' doubles as genitive). After PDF verification, GB409_14 and GB409_21 were resolved from '?' to 1. Three features remain uncertain ('?') due to limited scope of Santiago (2013): GB409_15, 19, 24. Glottocode ahin1234 is correct; the previously proposed kala1373 corresponds to Gawri (ISO gwc, Pakistan), an unrelated Indo-Aryan language.
